claims.text: Rapidly solidified FeNiCrMn contains nanoscale Mn2O3 precipitates.
The Mn2O3 precipitates form during rapid solidification.
Nanoscale Mn2O3 precipitates control the dynamic mechanical response of as-solidified FeNiCrMn.
At lower temperatures and moderate strain rates, Mn2O3 precipitates reinforce FeNiCrMn through Orowan strengthening.
At higher temperatures and strain rates, Mn2O3 precipitates exert Zener drag.
Zener drag from Mn2O3 precipitates delays dynamic recrystallization in FeNiCrMn.
Rapidly solidified FeNiCrMn has a fine-grained structure.
Rapidly solidified FeNiCrMn has a high dislocation density.
The Mn2O3 precipitates are uniformly distributed at cell boundaries in as-solidified FeNiCrMn.
The density, size, and distribution of Mn2O3 precipitates mediate both dislocation motion and grain-boundary mobility.
The combined Orowan and Zener-drag effects maintain strength and ductility across a range of temperatures and strain rates.
At low temperatures, precipitate strengthening produces high yield strength.
At intermediate or high temperatures and increased strain rates, FeNiCrMn will exhibit serrated yielding.
As-solidified FeNiCrMn will exhibit a later onset of dynamic recrystallization than precipitate-free or precipitate-coarsened material.
The mechanical response varies systematically with testing temperature.
Co-containing CoCrFeMnNi alloys exhibit a less pronounced role of nanoscale oxide precipitates in dynamic behavior than FeNiCrMn.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the nanoscale Mn2O3 precipitate dispersion is preserved in as-solidified or minimally heat-treated FeNiCrMn.
Extensive annealing can coarsen or dissolve the Mn2O3 precipitates and move the alloy outside the proposed regime.
